readings.title: Nathan's Parable
readings.subtitle: The Rich Man and the Poor Man's Lamb
readings.text: [2 Samuel 12:1] Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent <dn>את</dn> Nathan to Daviḏ. And he came to him, and said to him, “There were two men in one city, one rich and the other poor. [2] “The rich one had flocks and herds, very many. [3] “But the poor one had only one little ewe lamb which he had bought and kept alive. And it grew up with him and with his children together. It ate of his own food and drank from his own cup and lay in his bosom. And it was like a daughter to him. [4] “And a traveller came to the rich man, who refused to take from his own flock and from his own herd to prepare one for the wayfaring man who had come to him, but he took <dn>את</dn> the poor man’s lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him.” [5] And the wrath of Daviḏ burned greatly against the man, and he said to Nathan, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, the man who has done <dn>את</dn> this is a son of death! [6] “Also, he has to repay fourfold for the lamb, because he did <dn>את</dn> this deed and because he had no compassion.”

readings.title: You Are the Man
readings.subtitle: The Judgment Upon David's House
readings.text: [7] Then Nathan said to Daviḏ, “You are the man! Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> anointed you sovereign over Yisra’ěl, and <dn>I</dn> delivered you from the hand of Sha’ul.</dq> [8] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> gave you <dn>את</dn> your master’s house and <dn>את</dn> your master’s wives into your bosom, and gave you <dn>את</dn> the house of Yisra’ěl and Yehuḏah. And if that were not enough, <dn>I</dn> also would have given you much more!</dq> [9] <dq>Why have you despised <dn>את</dn> the Word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to do evil in <dn>His</dn> eyes? You have struck <dn>את</dn> Uriyah the Ḥittite with the sword, and <dn>את</dn> his wife you took to be your wife, and you have killed <dn>את</dn> him with the sword of the children of Ammon.</dq> [10] <dq>And now, the sword does not turn aside from your house, because you have despised <dn>Me</dn>, and have taken <dn>את</dn> the wife of Uriyah the Ḥittite to be your wife.’</dq> [11] “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘See, <dn>I</dn> am raising up evil against you, from your own house, and shall take <dn>את</dn> your wives before your eyes and give them to your neighbour, and he shall lie with <dn>את</dn> your wives in the sight of this sun.</dq> [12] <dq>For you did it in secret, but <dn>I</dn> shall do <dn>את</dn> this deed before all Yisra’ěl, and before the sun.’</dq> ”

readings.title: The Death of the Child
readings.subtitle: David Fasts and Pleads
readings.text: [13] And Daviḏ said to Nathan, “I have sinned against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” And Nathan said to Daviḏ, “Also, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has put away <dn>את</dn> your sin, you shall not die. [14] “However, because by this deed you have greatly scorned <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the child also who is born to you shall certainly die.” [15] And Nathan went to his house, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> smote <dn>את</dn> the child that Uriyah’s wife had born to Daviḏ, and he was sick. [16] And Daviḏ sought <dn>את</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> for the child, and Daviḏ fasted and went in and spent all night lying on the ground. [17] So the elders of his house stood up over him, to raise him up from the earth. But he would not, nor did he eat food with <dn>את</dn> them. [18] And on the seventh day it came to be that the child died. And the servants of Daviḏ were afraid to inform him that the child was dead, for they said, “Look, while the child was still alive, we spoke to him, and he would not listen to our voice. And how do we say to him that the child is dead? Then he shall do evil!”

readings.title: David Comforts Bathsheba
readings.subtitle: The Birth of Solomon
readings.text: [19] And Daviḏ saw that his servants were whispering, and Daviḏ perceived that the child was dead. Then Daviḏ said to his servants, “Is the child dead?” And they said, “He is dead.” [20] Daviḏ then rose up from the ground, and washed and anointed himself, and changed his garments. And he went into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and bowed himself, then came to his own house, and asked, and they set food before him, so he ate. [21] And his servants said to him, “What is this that you have done? You fasted and wept because of the living child, but when the child died, you rose up and ate food.” [22] And he said, “While the child was alive I fasted and wept, for I said, ‘Who knows whether <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shows favour unto me, and the child shall live?’ [23] “But now he is dead, why should I fast? Am I able to bring him back again? I am going to him, but he does not return to me.” [24] And Daviḏ comforted <dn>את</dn> Bathsheḇa his wife, and went in to her and lay with her. So she bore a son, and he called <dn>את</dn> his name Shelomoh. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> loved him, [25] and sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and called <dn>את</dn> his name Yeḏiḏeyah, because of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: Joab Captures Rabbah
readings.subtitle: David Takes the Crown of Ammon
readings.text: [26] And Yo’aḇ fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and captured <dn>את</dn> the royal city. [27] And Yo’aḇ sent messengers to Daviḏ, and said, “I have fought against Rabbah, and I have captured <dn>את</dn> the city’s water supply. [28] “And now, gather <dn>את</dn> the rest of the people together and encamp against the city and capture it, lest I capture <dn>את</dn> the city and it be called after my name.” [29] And Daviḏ gathered <dn>את</dn> all the people and went to Rabbah, and fought against it, and captured it. [30] And he took <dn>את</dn> their sovereign’s crown from his head. And its weight was a talent of gold, with precious stones, and it was on Daviḏ’s head. And he brought out the spoil of the city, a very great amount. [31] And he brought out <dn>את</dn> the people who were in it, and set them to the saw and to sharp instruments of iron and to axes of iron, and made them pass over to the brick works. And so he did with all the cities of the children of Ammon. And Daviḏ and all the people returned to Yerushalayim.

readings.title: The Defeat of Ammon
readings.subtitle: David's Victory and Spoils
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 20:1] And it came to be at the turn of the year, at the time sovereigns go out to battle, that Yo’aḇ led out <dn>את</dn> the power of the army and destroyed <dn>את</dn> the land of the children of Ammon, and came and besieged <dn>את</dn> Rabbah. But Daviḏ remained at Yerushalayim. And Yo’aḇ struck <dn>את</dn> Rabbah and overthrew it. [2] And Daviḏ took <dn>את</dn> their sovereign’s crown from his head, and found it weighed a talent of gold, and there were precious stones in it. And it was set on Daviḏ’s head. And he also brought out the spoil of the city, a very great amount. [3] And he brought out <dn>את</dn> the people who were in it, and put them to work with saws, and with iron picks, and with axes. And thus Daviḏ did to all the cities of the children of Ammon. Then Daviḏ and all the people returned to Yerushalayim.

readings.title: Battles Against the Philistine Giants
readings.subtitle: The Defeat of Goliath's Brother
readings.text: [4] And afterward it came to be that fighting broke out at Gezer with the Philistines. Then Sibbeḵai the Ḥushathite struck <dn>את</dn> Sippai of the sons of the giant, and they were humbled. [5] And there was fighting again with the Philistines, and Elḥanan son of Ya’ir struck <dn>את</dn> Laḥmi the brother of Golyath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam. [6] And there was fighting again at Gath, where there was a man of great size, with twenty-four fingers and toes, six and six. And he too was born to the giant. [7] And he reproached <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl, and Yehonathan son of Shim‛a, Daviḏ’s brother, struck him. [8] These were born to the giant in Gath, and they fell by the hand of Daviḏ and by the hand of his servants.

readings.title: Amnon's Deception
readings.subtitle: The Defilement of Tamar
readings.text: [2 Samuel 13:1] And after this it came to be that Aḇshalom son of Daviḏ had a beautiful sister, whose name was Tamar, and Amnon son of Daviḏ loved her. [2] And Amnon was distressed, even to become sick, because of his sister Tamar – for she was a maiden – and it was hard in the eyes of Amnon to do whatever to her. [3] And Amnon had a friend whose name was Yonaḏaḇ son of Shim‛ah, Daviḏ’s brother. Now Yonaḏaḇ was a very wise man. [4] And he said to him, “Why are you, the sovereign’s son, becoming thinner day after day? Explain it to me.” And Amnon said to him, “I love <dn>את</dn> Tamar, my brother Aḇshalom’s sister.” [5] And Yonaḏaḇ said to him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. And when your father comes to see you, say to him, ‘Please let my sister Tamar come and give me food, and make <dn>את</dn> the food before my eyes so that I see it, and eat it from her hand.’ ” [6] So Amnon lay down and pretended to be sick. And when the sovereign came to see him, Amnon said to the sovereign, “Please let Tamar my sister come and make a couple of cakes for me before my eyes, so that I eat from her hand.” [7] And Daviḏ sent to Tamar, to the house, saying, “Please go to the house of your brother Amnon, and make food for him.” [8] So Tamar went to her brother Amnon’s house, while he was lying down. And she took <dn>את</dn> dough and kneaded it, and made cakes before his eyes, and baked <dn>את</dn> the cakes. [9] And she took <dn>את</dn> the pan and turned them out before him, but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, “Make everyone go away from me.” And they all went out from him. [10] And Amnon said to Tamar, “Bring the food into the bedroom, that I eat from your hand.” And Tamar took <dn>את</dn> the cakes which she had made, and brought them to Amnon her brother in the bedroom. [11] And she brought them to him to eat, and he took hold of her and said to her, “Come, lie with <dn>את</dn> me, my sister.” [12] And she answered him, “No, my brother, do not humble me, for it is not done so in Yisra’ěl. Do not do <dn>את</dn> this wickedness! [13] “And I, where could I take <dn>את</dn> my shame? And you – you would be like one of the fools in Yisra’ěl. And now, please speak to the sovereign, for he would not withhold me from you.” [14] But he would not listen to her voice, and being stronger than she, he humbled her and lay with <dn>את</dn> her.

readings.title: Amnon's Hatred
readings.subtitle: Tamar's Desolation
readings.text: [15] Amnon then hated her exceedingly, so that the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her. And Amnon said to her, “Arise, go!” [16] And she said to him, “No, for this evil of sending me away is worse than the other you have done to me.” But he would not listen to her. [17] And he called <dn>את</dn> his young man serving him, and said, “Now put <dn>את</dn> this one out, away from me, and bolt the door behind her.” [18] And she had on a long coat, for the sovereign’s maiden daughters wore such garments. And his servant put her out and bolted the door behind her. [19] And Tamar put ashes on her head, and tore her long coat that was on her, and put her hand on her head and went away crying bitterly. [20] And Aḇshalom her brother said to her, “Has Amnon your brother been with you? But now, keep silent, my sister. He is your brother, do not take this matter to heart.” So Tamar remained in the house of her brother Aḇshalom, but was ruined. [21] And Sovereign Daviḏ heard <dn>את</dn> all these reports, and he was very wroth. [22] And Aḇshalom spoke to his brother Amnon neither good nor evil. For Aḇshalom hated <dn>את</dn> Amnon, because he had humbled <dn>את</dn> his sister Tamar.

readings.title: Absalom's Revenge
readings.subtitle: The Murder of Amnon
readings.text: [23] And it came to be, after two years, that Aḇshalom had sheep-shearers in Ba‛al Hatsor, which is beside Ephrayim, and Aḇshalom invited all the sons of the sovereign. [24] And Aḇshalom came to the sovereign and said, “See, your servant has sheep-shearers. Please, let the sovereign and his servants go with <dn>את</dn> your servant.” [25] But the sovereign said to Aḇshalom, “No, my son, let us not all go now, lest we be too heavy on you.” And he urged him, but he would not go. And he blessed him. [26] And Aḇshalom said, “If not, please let my brother Amnon go with <dn>את</dn> us.” And the sovereign said to him, “Why should he go with you?” [27] And Aḇshalom urged him, so he let <dn>את</dn> Amnon and <dn>את</dn> all the sons of the sovereign go with <dn>את</dn> him. [28] And Aḇshalom had commanded <dn>את</dn> his servants, saying, “Watch, and when the heart of Amnon is glad with wine, and I shall say to you, ‘Strike <dn>את</dn> Amnon!’ then kill him. Do not be afraid. Have I not commanded you? Be strong and brave.” [29] Then the servants of Aḇshalom did to Amnon as Aḇshalom had commanded. Then all the sons of the sovereign rose up, and each one mounted his mule and fled.

readings.title: David Mourns for Amnon
readings.subtitle: Absalom Flees to Geshur
readings.text: [30] And it came to be, while they were on the way, that news came to Daviḏ, saying, “Aḇshalom has stricken <dn>את</dn> all the sons of the sovereign, and not one of them is left!” [31] And the sovereign rose up and tore <dn>את</dn> his garments and lay on the ground, and all his servants stood by with their garments torn. [32] And Yonaḏaḇ son of Shim‛ah, Daviḏ’s brother, answered and said, “Do not let my master say they have killed <dn>את</dn> all the young men, the sons of the sovereign, for only Amnon is dead. For by the mouth of Aḇshalom this has been appointed from the day that he humbled <dn>את</dn> his sister Tamar. [33] “And now, let not my master the sovereign take the matter to his heart, to think that all the sons of the sovereign are dead. For only Amnon is dead.” [34] And Aḇshalom fled, and the young man who was watching lifted up <dn>את</dn> his eyes and looked and saw many people were coming from the way behind him, on the side of the hill. [35] Then Yonaḏaḇ said to the sovereign, “Look, the sons of the sovereign are coming; as your servant said, so it is.” [36] And it came to be, as soon as he had finished speaking, that look, the sons of the sovereign came, and they lifted up their voice and wept. And the sovereign too, and all his servants wept very bitterly. [37] But Aḇshalom fled and went to Talmai son of Ammihuḏ, sovereign of Geshur. And Daviḏ mourned for his son all the days. [38] So Aḇshalom fled and went to Geshur, and was there three years. [39] Sovereign Daviḏ then longed to go to Aḇshalom, for he had been comforted concerning Amnon, because he was dead.

readings.title: The Wise Woman of Tekoa
readings.subtitle: A Parable for the King
readings.text: [2 Samuel 14:1] And Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah knew that the heart of the sovereign was towards Aḇshalom. [2] And Yo’aḇ sent to Teqova and brought from there a wise woman, and said to her, “Please pretend to be a mourner, and put on mourning garments, and do not anoint yourself with oil, but act like a woman who has been mourning a long time for the dead. [3] “Then you shall go to the sovereign and speak to him according to this word.” And Yo’aḇ put <dn>את</dn> the words in her mouth. [4] And when the woman of Teqova spoke to the sovereign, she fell on her face to the ground and did obeisance, and said, “Save, O sovereign!” [5] And the sovereign said to her, “What is your trouble?” And she answered, “Truly I am a widow, my husband is dead. [6] “And your female servant had two sons. And the two fought with each other in the field, and there was no one to part them, but the one struck <dn>את</dn> the other and killed him. [7] “And see, the entire clan has risen up against your female servant and said, ‘Give <dn>את</dn> him who struck his brother, so that we put him to death for the life of his brother whom he killed, and destroy <dn>את</dn> the heir also.’ Thus they would extinguish <dn>את</dn> my burning coal that is left, and leave to my husband neither name nor remnant on the earth.” [8] And the sovereign said to the woman, “Go to your house, and let me give commands concerning you.” [9] And the woman of Teqova said to the sovereign, “My master, O sovereign, let the crookedness be on me and on my father’s house, and the sovereign and his throne be guiltless.” [10] And the sovereign said, “Whoever speaks to you, bring him to me, and let him no longer touch you.” [11] And she said, “Please let the sovereign remember <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and the redeemer of blood not destroy any more, lest they destroy <dn>את</dn> my son.” And he said, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, not one hair of your son shall fall to the ground.”

readings.title: The Woman's Plea
readings.subtitle: Joab's Hand Revealed
readings.text: [12] And the woman said, “Please, let your female servant speak a word to my master the sovereign.” And he said, “Speak.” [13] And the woman said, “And why have you reasoned like this against the people of <dn>Elohim</dn>? For in speaking this word the sovereign is as one who is guilty, in that the sovereign does not bring <dn>את</dn> his outcast one home again. [14] “For we shall certainly die and become like water spilled on the ground, which is not gathered up again. Yet <dn>Elohim</dn> does not take away a life, but shall devise ways, so that <dn>His</dn> outcast ones are not cast out from <dn>Him</dn>. [15] “And now I have come to speak <dn>את</dn> this word to my master the sovereign because the people have made me afraid. And your female servant said, ‘Please let me speak to the sovereign, it could be that the sovereign does <dn>את</dn> what his female servant asks, [16] for the sovereign has listened to deliver <dn>את</dn> his female servant from the hand of the man seeking to destroy <dn>את</dn> me and <dn>את</dn> my son together from the inheritance of <dn>Elohim</dn>.’ [17] “Then your female servant said, ‘Please let the word of my master the sovereign be comforting, for my master the sovereign is as the messenger of <dn>Elohim</dn>, in discerning the good and the evil. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is with <dn>את</dn> you.’ ” [18] And the sovereign answered and said to the woman, “Please do not hide from me the matter that I am asking you.” And the woman said, “Please, let my master the sovereign speak.” [19] And the sovereign said, “Is the hand of Yo’aḇ with <dn>את</dn> you in all this?” And the woman answered and said, “As your being lives, my master the sovereign, no one turns to the right or to the left from all that my master the sovereign has spoken. For your servant Yo’aḇ commanded me, and he put <dn>את</dn> all these words in the mouth of your female servant. [20] “Your servant Yo’aḇ has done <dn>את</dn> this to change <dn>את</dn> the appearance of the matter. But my master is wise, according to the wisdom of a messenger of <dn>Elohim</dn>, to know <dn>את</dn> all that is in the earth.”

readings.title: Absalom Returns to Jerusalem
readings.subtitle: The Beauty of Absalom
readings.text: [21] And the sovereign said to Yo’aḇ, “See now, you shall do <dn>את</dn> this matter. And go, bring back <dn>את</dn> the young man <dn>את</dn> Aḇshalom.” [22] And Yo’aḇ fell to the ground on his face and did obeisance, and blessed <dn>את</dn> the sovereign. And Yo’aḇ said, “Today your servant knows that I have found favour in your eyes, my master, O sovereign, in that the sovereign has done <dn>את</dn> the word of his servant.” [23] And Yo’aḇ rose up and went to Geshur, and brought <dn>את</dn> Aḇshalom to Yerushalayim. [24] And the sovereign said, “Let him return to his own house, but do not let him see my face.” And Aḇshalom went to his own house, and did not see the sovereign’s face. [25] And in all Yisra’ěl there was no one who was praised as much as Aḇshalom for his handsomeness. From the sole of his foot to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him. [26] And when he cut <dn>את</dn> the hair of his head – for it was at every year’s end that he cut it because it was heavy on him – when he cut it, he weighed <dn>את</dn> the hair of his head at two hundred sheqels by the sovereign’s weight. [27] And to Aḇshalom were born three sons, and one daughter whose name was Tamar. She was a woman of beautiful appearance.

readings.title: Absalom Demands an Audience
readings.subtitle: David Forgives Absalom
readings.text: [28] And Aḇshalom dwelt in Yerushalayim, two years, and he had not seen the sovereign’s face. [29] Then Aḇshalom sent for Yo’aḇ, to send <dn>את</dn> him to the sovereign, but he would not come to him. And he sent again the second time, but he would not come. [30] And he said to his servants, “See, Yo’aḇ’s field is near mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire.” And Aḇshalom’s servants set <dn>את</dn> the field on fire. [31] Then Yo’aḇ rose up and came to the house of Aḇshalom, and said to him, “Why have your servants set <dn>את</dn> my field on fire?” [32] And Aḇshalom said to Yo’aḇ, “Look, I sent to you, saying, ‘Come here, so that I send <dn>את</dn> you to the sovereign, to say, “Why have I come from Geshur? It was good for me while I was there.” ’ And now, let me see the sovereign’s face. And if there is any crookedness in me, then you shall put me to death.” [33] Yo’aḇ then went to the sovereign and informed him. And he called for Aḇshalom, and he came to the sovereign and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the sovereign. Then the sovereign kissed Aḇshalom.
